default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-668.title: Round-number level rejection
E-668.hypothesis: Stop and limit orders cluster at round index/dollar levels; a bar that pokes through a round level and closes back on the near side has run those stops without follow-through, so fade it.

E-669.title: Three-bar low/high sweep reversal
E-669.hypothesis: A bar that sweeps below the two previous lows and closes above the previous high traps sellers; buy it (mirror for sells), only when the bar is not tiny.

E-670.title: Narrowest-range bar breakout
E-670.hypothesis: When the previous bar has the smallest range of the last n bars, volatility is compressed; a close beyond its high/low starts the expansion in that direction.

E-671.title: Floor-pivot cross with EMA side
E-671.hypothesis: The previous session's pivot (H+L+C)/3 is a reference many desks use; a fresh cross of it that agrees with the short EMA side signals a bias shift for the session.

E-672.title: Day-open retest bounce
E-672.hypothesis: After the session has traded well away from its opening price, the first retest of the open is a level of unfinished business; buyers/sellers who drove the move defend it, so follow the original side.

E-674.title: Close-location volume flow cross
E-674.hypothesis: Volume weighted by where each bar closes in its range measures who finished each bar in control; a cross of the n-bar flow above a threshold marks aggressive persistent buying (or selling).

E-675.title: Hour-end drift follow
E-675.hypothesis: Index and dollar flow tied to hourly rebalancing and algorithmic hourly benchmarks tends to push in the direction of the hour's move into its last 10 minutes; trade with it at minute :50.

E-676.title: Range-midline cross follow
E-676.hypothesis: The midpoint of the recent high-low range is the balance point of a Donchian channel; closing across it after trading on the other side shows supply or demand has taken over.

E-677.title: Tweezer reversal after a push
E-677.hypothesis: Two successive bars of opposite colour stopping at the same high (or low) after a push show a defended level; the pushers are rejected twice, so fade.
